misattributed.line: Sayings credited to Poemen in general
misattributed.truth: Some sayings under his name may belong to other monks named Poemen or be misassigned; Budge's Syriac marks a few with "(or Ammon)". No specific fake was found.

opinions.position: Do not punish or shame the weak; cover for them.
opinions.side_note: Correction: extremely gentle.
opinions.quote: If I see my brother sleeping, I place his head upon my knees, and I give him a place to rest upon
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Split. Many admire this; others think people need correcting.

opinions.position: If you see a brother sinning, pass by and do not see it.
opinions.side_note: Correction: against rebuking others.
opinions.quote: If I had some business which made me pass by him, and in passing by him I saw him committing sin, I should pass him by and not see him.
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Strongly split. Many say love means speaking up. Good quiz material.

opinions.position: The aim is to kill passions, not the body. He washed his feet and ate a little every day rather than fasting for days.
opinions.side_note: Asceticism: moderate.
opinions.quote: We have not learned to be slayers of the body, but slayers of the passions.
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.location: Book II, Questions and Answers on the Rule of Life, no. 166
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Most agree today. The contrast with Antony and Arsenius makes it useful.

opinions.position: Being angry at someone who wrongs you, even cruelly, is anger without cause. The only right anger is at someone who tries to take you away from God.
opinions.side_note: Anger: allows it only in defence of your faith.
opinions.quote: but if a man wisheth to separate thee or to put thee away from God, then to be angry and wroth with him is a good thing.
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Split. Many think anger at injustice is healthy; he rules out anger over personal wrongs.

opinions.position: Deep grief cannot be cheered away by music; a monk should carry grief for sin like that.
opinions.side_note: Grief: takes mourning seriously and uses it as a model.
opinions.quote: If every kind of instrument of sweet music in the world were to come [here] they would not be able to change the grief of this woman’s soul [into gladness]
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Most people agree grief cannot be cheered away. The idea of carrying grief for sin splits.

opinions.position: Monks must not let family ties pull them back; he refused his sister and told the judge to try her son by law.
opinions.side_note: Family-calling: puts calling far above kin.
opinions.quote: Examine and consider his case according to the Law, and if he be worthy of death, let him die
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Most people today put family first. Strongly one-sided against him; a strong sparring point.

opinions.topic: new: hospitality to those you disagree with
opinions.position: Feed heretics who insult your bishop and send them off in peace, without arguing.
opinions.side_note: Kindness over debate (contrast with Antony, who drove Arians away).
opinions.quote: Make ready a table and make them eat
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Most agree today. Some believers would want to correct them.

opinions.position: Silence is inner: a quiet man who judges others is talking all the time, and a talker without judgment is silent.
opinions.side_note: Silence: redefines it as not condemning.
opinions.quote: One man is thought to be silent, yet his heart condemneth others, and he who is thus speaketh everything; and another speaketh from morn until evening, and yet keepeth silence
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Most would agree once they hear it.

opinions.position: On an inheritance: the church will spend it on feasts, relatives bring no reward, the poor are best, but in the end, do as you like.
opinions.side_note: Wealth: sceptical of giving to the church.
opinions.quote: If I tell thee to give it to the church, they will make feasts with it
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Split. Many people today distrust giving to churches; church members disagree.

opinions.position: Remind a debtor once. If he does not pay, let it go; do not harass him.
opinions.side_note: Forgiving debts.
opinions.quote: Let the thought perish, only do not harass the man.
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Split. Most people would keep asking for their money.

opinions.position: He told a monk who had handed robbers to the governor to get them released.
opinions.side_note: Against using the law against those who wrong you.
opinions.quote: for if thou hadst not been betrayed first of all by those that were within thou wouldst never have effected the second betrayal.
opinions.work: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Syriac collection, in Budge, The Paradise, vol. 2)
opinions.location: Book II, Questions and Answers on the Rule of Life, no. 49
opinions.translation: E. A. Wallis Budge, The Paradise or Garden of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), from the Syriac collection of ʿAnan-Isho; Wikisource transcription
opinions.today: Most people today would press charges against burglars. Strongly split.

sparring.over: Washing his feet; Isaac thought it soft, Poemen said the goal was to kill passions, not the body.
sparring.source: Budge, The Paradise vol. 2, Questions and Answers on the Rule of Life, no. 166

sparring.over: Her son jailed by a judge; she called him "thou who possessest mercy of brass"; he would not intervene.
sparring.source: Budge, The Paradise vol. 2, Book I, ch. 8, no. 265

sparring.with: Old monks who wanted to strike sleepers
sparring.over: Discipline in church; he rested the sleeper's head on his knees.
sparring.source: Budge, The Paradise vol. 2, Book I, ch. 9, no. 443

sparring.over: Paesius befriended people outside the monastery; Poemen disapproved and complained to Abba Ammon.
sparring.source: Budge, The Paradise vol. 2, Book I, ch. 6, no. 236
